newsitem.title: UK: Girl, 12, released from Isle of Man prison.
newsitem.headline: Girl, 12, released from Isle of Man prison.

text.p: Isle of Man authorities have released from jail a 12-year-old girl being held on assault charges.
Her case sparked outrage from British human rights activists who complained to the U.N. Committee on the Rights of the Child.
The child was released from jail on the island, a dependency of the British crown located in the Irish Sea off northwestern England, into the care of a children's home on Tuesday night.
Her lawyer, Terence McDonald, told Britain's Independent newspaper: "I welcome it but feel it is a great pity that something could not have been done sooner."
"The police are not looking into the circumstances of juveniles and are treating child offenders like adults. They are exaggerating the juvenile delinquency by charging so many young people."
Manx authorities said the island's law provided for the imprisonment of children as young as 12 in exceptional circumstances. The girl in this case had been strictly segregated from adult prisoners.
The child had been accused of assaulting social workers.
The Isle of Man has a reputation for taking a hard line on law and order. The death penalty was only abolished in 1993 and punishment by the birch remains on the statute book.
